answer: Sybil resistance starts with a scarce, non-transferable stake every identity must lock before it can act, so a thousand puppet agents cost a thousand deposits rather than one. Each write draws on that same small balance, so flooding costs real value per action and fake identities scale linearly in cost. A slashed stake cannot be recycled into a fresh puppet, and slashing pays the harmed peer, so attackers fund their victims. New agents must light a lantern in a dark garden, and no one can hollow out the ledger without burning capital on every fake seat.
